messages:
mike: Heads-up: saw a 2.8% p99 tail latency regression on mistral-8x7b after yesterday's runtime change. Pattern looks correlated with long context rolls past 2048 tokens (sliding-window).
anya: ugh. which change specifically? kernel selector tweak?
mike: yeah, the kernel selector now prefers the fused-atten kernel for sequences >= 2048. CPU profile shows extra memcpy spikes around KV writes.
sylvie: can you paste the perf traces?
mike: copied snippets: 
```
[perf] timeline: dispatch_kernel(fused-atten) -> memcpy(kv_write) -> kernel_complete -> serialize_batch
avg memcpy per request: 1.2ms when seq>2048, 0.3ms otherwise
```

mike: also seeing more small-batch flushes in batching logs when clients send rolling windows: the batcher emits 2-6 smaller batches instead of one consolidated.
rahul: that smells like KV cache fragmentation + batch queuing contention. If fused-atten writes KV differently we might break our KV-page alignment heuristic.
tz: did we change the KV tile size or tiling alignment with the kernel swap?
mike: kernel's write uses 64B granularity vs old 256B assumption. allocator still aligned to 256B -> extra padding + more frequent page commits.
anya: interesting. could cause additional PCIe small transfers and queueing. bench-bot: run scheduled microbench for kv-write-size distribution (1796552100)
bench-bot: results: avg transfer size upstream: 48B for affected ops, median 56B, tail 1KB. overall transfer count +45% for rolling-window workloads.
sylvie: ok that explains memcpy spikes. What about pos embeddings / RoPE? you mentioned crossing 2048 boundary earlier.
mike: right — model max_position_embeddings reported as 4096 in model config, but we have a legacy path that applies RoPE scaling only up to 2048 without wrap-check. When seq slides beyond 2048, we hit the 'poswrap' codepath that re-allocs for KV and triggers extra copies.
rahul: so two compounding things: kernel changed write granularity -> more small transfers, and poswrap path forces KV rebase -> batcher flushes.
tz: can we short-circuit poswrap for Mistral 8x7b by mapping positions mod 4096 without full rebase? maybe a lazy remap in the attention kernel.
anya: we could also tweak batching heuristics to avoid mid-request flushes: increase max_batch_window_ms for sliding-window routes, or add a soft-prefix-coalesce that tries to merge micro-batches for identical prefix lengths.
mike: quick experiment: patched kernel selector to prefer the older kernel for seq in [2048,3072) and left fused-atten for >=3072. local repro shows p99 back to baseline but throughput drops ~1.1% at high concurrency.
sylvie: tradeoff acceptable if tail latency improves for customer-facing endpoints. Any way to keep fused kernel but modify KV write path?
rahul: probable fix: update allocator alignment to 64B for affected allocs and add batched write coalescing in runtime. Should reduce transfer count without regressing fused kernel's compute perf.
tz: also add an explicit check: if model.max_position_embeddings >= seq_len then bypass poswrap rebase entirely. We accidentally treat >= as < in one branch earlier.
anya: nice catch — that off-by-one would only show up when seq hits exactly the configured boundary.
mike: I'll open a small PR with three changes: 1) allocator alignment for kernel-chosen path, 2) batching heuristic tweak (soft coalesce, +10ms window for sliding-window tag), 3) fix poswrap boundary check.
rahul: call out risk: alignment change could increase memory usage a bit; quantify in PR.
sylvie: can you also add a simple perf test in ci that exercises sliding-window sequences with client interleaving? We lack regression coverage there.
mike: will add. Patch queued: https://review.redwood/mike/poswrap-kv-align (WIP)
bench-bot: quick sandbox microbench (post-patch candidate): p99 latency -2.9%, throughput -0.6%, memcpy ops -42% for sliding-window workload.
deploy-bot: note: next canary planned for eng-runtime tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Are we comfortable canarying with these changes?
anya: yes but gate on canary metrics: p50/p95/p99 and memcpy-count + io-wait.
sylvie: also add a regression alert for 'batch flush rate' metric spike.
rahul: one more thought — for Mistral 7B vs 8x7b the kv dims differ; make allocator change keyed by (model, kv_dim) so we don't over-shrink for eg Llama configs that rely on 256 alignment.
mike: good call. I'll parameterize and add a mapping.
tz: anyone seen head/kv-dim mismatch causing kernel selector to pick a suboptimal kernel? Might be relevant when model variants are served behind the same route.
anya: yes we've seen that: kernel heuristics assume head dim divisibility by 64; add a small gap penalty when divisibility is poor.
mike: summary of action items I will do: (1) PR with alignment + poswrap boundary fix + batching tweak, (2) add sliding-window ci test, (3) add canary gating rules, (4) bench more kv-dim matrix combos.
sylvie: thanks. if bench numbers hold, roll to canary and monitor. please ping #incidents if anything odd. :slightly_smiling_face:
rahul: +1
tz: +1
anya: thanks mike.
bench-bot: archived microbench logs to /artifacts/179655/poswrap-kv-bench.tgz
deploy-bot: scheduled canary at 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z (job id: canary-179655-01)
mike: will follow up with PR link and a short postmortem after canary.
